summary: Establish DonationHub: Clean Architecture, Rich Domain Model, JWT Identity, and the Categories module.

briefBlocks.text: Sprint 1 — Clean Architecture, Domain Modeling, Identity & Categories

briefBlocks.markdown: In this sprint, you lay the **architectural foundation** for **DonationHub** — a donation and charity campaign management platform. Everything you build in upcoming sprints (CQRS, Donations, Stripe, Hangfire, Docker) rests on what you establish now, so quality here matters more than speed.
- **Evaluation:** 100 Points
**Target Framework:** .NET 10 (`net10.0`) with the `.slnx` solution format and all configuration in `Program.cs`. The project is also compatible with .NET 8 and .NET 9.

Build a four-layer Clean Architecture solution, organized internally using **Vertical Slices**, with an EF Core persistence layer (Fluent API + Migrations + Interceptors), and deliver two fully working modules:

1. **Identity:** Registration, login, JWT, and Refresh Token rotation.
2. **Categories:** Bilingual category management with domain rules.

briefBlocks.code:
Domain Model (Entities + Invariants + Value Objects)
        ↓
Clean Architecture (4 Layers + Dependency Inversion)
        ↓
Vertical Slice Organization inside Application Layer
        ↓
EF Core Persistence (Fluent API + Migrations + Interceptors)
        ↓
Secure & Documented API (JWT Bearer + Scalar / Swagger)

| **Domain Modeling** | Rich Domain Model | Anemic models are prohibited. Setters are private (`private set`). Business rules live inside entities, with Value Objects to prevent Primitive Obsession. |
| **Soft Delete** | Interceptor-Driven | Entities implement `ISoftDeletable`, and `SoftDeleteInterceptor` converts `EntityState.Deleted` to `IsDeleted = true`, with a global query filter `HasQueryFilter(e => !e.IsDeleted)`. |
| **Configuration** | Options Pattern | Strongly-typed option classes, validated with Data Annotations at startup via `.ValidateOnStart()`. |

briefBlocks.markdown: Model the domain entities per SRS §4.1 (all IDs are `Guid` and all timestamps are UTC):

- `ApplicationUser` (Identity user): `Id`, `Email`, `UserName`, `FullName`, `PreferredLanguage` (`en` | `ar`, default `en`), `IsActive`, `CreatedAt`. Roles: `Admin`, `CampaignManager`, `Donor`.
- `RefreshToken`: `Id`, `UserId`, `TokenHash`, `CreatedAt`, `ExpiresAt`, `RevokedAt?`, `ReplacedByTokenId?`.
- `Category`: `Id`, `NameAr`, `NameEn`, `DescriptionAr`, `DescriptionEn`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`.
- `Campaign`: `Id`, `TitleAr`, `TitleEn`, `DescriptionAr`, `DescriptionEn`, `GoalAmount`, `RaisedAmount`, `EndDate`, `CategoryId`, `BannerFileName?`, `Status`, `CreatedByUserId`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`, `IsDeleted`, `RowVersion`.
- `Donation`: `Id`, `CampaignId`, `DonorUserId`, `Amount`, `Status`, `CreatedAt`, `CompletedAt?`, `FailureReason?`, `ReceiptNumber?`, `ReceiptFileName?`.
- `PaymentAttempt`: `Id`, `DonationId`, `StripeCheckoutSessionId`, `StripePaymentIntentId?`, `Amount`, `Status`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`, `FailureCode?`.
- `ProcessedStripeEvent`: `EventId` (key), `Type`, `ProcessedAt`.
- `IdempotencyRecord`: `Key`, `UserId`, `RequestHash`, `ResponseStatusCode`, `ResponseBody`, `CreatedAt`, `ExpiresAt`.

**Enums:** `CampaignStatus` (Active, Completed, Expired) — `DonationStatus` (Pending, Succeeded, Failed) — `PaymentAttemptStatus` (Created, Succeeded, Failed, Expired).

**Value Objects:** Create a `ValueObject` base class with value-based equality comparison, and implement Value Objects where appropriate (such as `Money` encapsulating amount and currency).

**Domain Invariants (SRS §4.5)** — Model **all of them now** even if some are only exercised by endpoints later:

1. `GoalAmount > 0`.
2. `EndDate` must be in the future when a campaign is created or its end date is changed.
3. A campaign accepts a new donation only when `Status == Active` and `EndDate` is in the future. *(exercised in Sprint 3)*
4. Donation amount is within the minimum and maximum from `DonationOptions` (defaults: 1.00 and 10,000.00). *(Sprint 3)*
5. `RaisedAmount` changes only when a donation becomes `Succeeded`. *(Sprint 3)*
6. When `RaisedAmount >= GoalAmount` after a donation succeeds, the campaign becomes `Completed`. *(Sprint 3)*
7. `GoalAmount` cannot be lowered below the current `RaisedAmount`. *(Sprint 2)*
8. A final state (Succeeded, Failed, Completed, Expired) cannot change.
9. A campaign that has donations cannot be hard-deleted; use soft delete. *(Sprint 2)*
10. A category that still has campaigns cannot be deleted. *(enforced in this sprint via CAT-04)*

items: All setters are private (`private set`), and behavior is exposed via entity methods and factory methods such as `Campaign.Create(...)`.

Do not call `DateTime.UtcNow` inside the Domain; pass the current time as a parameter (`TimeProvider` will be injected into handlers starting in Sprint 2).

briefBlocks.text: Task 7 — Authentication & Identity (ASP.NET Core Identity & JWT)

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement the identity requirements from SRS §5.1:

items: **IDN-01:** Registration `POST /auth/register` with Email, FullName, Password, and `PreferredLanguage` (`en` | `ar`, default `en`). The new user gets the `Donor` role.
**IDN-02:** Password policy (at least 8 characters, upper case, lower case, digit), and case-insensitive unique email check (`Auth.EmailAlreadyExists` — 409).
**IDN-03 & IDN-04:** Login `POST /auth/login` returns a short-lived Access Token (15 minutes, configurable) with claims (UserId, Email, Roles) along with a secure Refresh Token.

**IDN-05 & IDN-06:** Refresh Token rotation: its lifetime is 7 days (configurable) and it is stored **hashed** in the database. When `/auth/refresh` is called, the old token is revoked (`RevokedAt`) and linked to the new one (`ReplacedByTokenId`). An invalid, expired, or revoked token returns `Auth.RefreshTokenInvalid` (401).
**IDN-07:** Logout `POST /auth/logout` revokes the supplied Refresh Token.
**IDN-08:** Admin endpoint to create staff users `POST /admin/staff` (roles `Admin` or `CampaignManager`) with a temporary password. Managing the rest of staff comes in Sprint 6.
**IDN-09:** Current user profile `GET /auth/me`.
**IDN-10:** Deactivated users (`IsActive = false`) are prohibited from logging in or refreshing tokens (`Auth.AccountDeactivated` — 403).
**IDN-11:** Seed initial Admin user at startup from `SeedAdminOptions` (never a hard-coded password).
**IDN-12:** Return the same generic error (`Auth.InvalidCredentials` — 401) whether the email or the password is wrong, to prevent User Enumeration attacks.

**Seed data (SRS §9.1, development only):** roles `Admin`, `CampaignManager`, and `Donor`; one Admin from options; one Campaign Manager and one Donor test user (credentials from user-secrets); five categories with Arabic and English names (e.g., Health, Education, Relief, Orphans, Environment).

briefBlocks.markdown:
| Method | Path | Access | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/auth/register` | Anonymous | Register a donor |
| `POST` | `/auth/login` | Anonymous | Login |
| `POST` | `/auth/refresh` | Anonymous | Rotate tokens |
| `POST` | `/auth/logout` | Any authenticated user | Revoke Refresh Token |
| `GET` | `/auth/me` | Any authenticated user | Current profile |
| `POST` | `/admin/staff` | Admin only | Create Admin or Campaign Manager |

All routes start with `/api/v1`.

Until the Result Pattern arrives in Sprint 2, return these error codes consistently from your endpoints: `Auth.InvalidCredentials` (401), `Auth.EmailAlreadyExists` (409), `Auth.RefreshTokenInvalid` (401), `Auth.AccountDeactivated` (403).

briefBlocks.markdown: Implement the category endpoints and rules from SRS §5.2:

solutionBlocks.markdown: This is a reference solution illustrating a sound **approach** for each task, not the only possible one. Compare your solution against it, and focus on the **rationale** behind each decision since you will be asked about it during review. The examples are written for .NET 10 with SQL Server and Controllers.

To keep things concise, some similar classes (such as `PaymentAttempt`, `IdempotencyRecord`, and their configurations) are not written out in full — build them following the same style as the entities shown.
We start with the CLI so the setup is repeatable. Notice that `Api` does not depend on `Domain` directly for business decisions, and `Domain` knows nothing about any other layer.

solutionBlocks.code:
mkdir DonationHub && cd DonationHub
dotnet new sln -n DonationHub --format slnx

dotnet new classlib -n DonationHub.Domain         -o src/DonationHub.Domain
dotnet new classlib -n DonationHub.Application    -o src/DonationHub.Application
dotnet new classlib -n DonationHub.Infrastructure -o src/DonationHub.Infrastructure
dotnet new webapi   -n DonationHub.Api            -o src/DonationHub.Api --use-controllers

dotnet sln add src/*/*.csproj

dotnet add src/DonationHub.Application/DonationHub.Application.csproj reference src/DonationHub.Domain/DonationHub.Domain.csproj
dotnet add src/DonationHub.Infrastructure/DonationHub.Infrastructure.csproj reference src/DonationHub.Application/DonationHub.Application.csproj src/DonationHub.Domain/DonationHub.Domain.csproj
dotnet add src/DonationHub.Api/DonationHub.Api.csproj reference src/DonationHub.Application/DonationHub.Application.csproj src/DonationHub.Infrastructure/DonationHub.Infrastructure.csproj

solutionBlocks.markdown: Each layer registers its own services, keeping `Program.cs` short so it only knows "what" is registered, not "how":

The `Infrastructure` project is a classlib, so add `<FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />` to its `.csproj` to access Identity Core and Options, then install `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer`, and `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer` (which are not part of the shared framework). Meanwhile, `Domain` remains with zero PackageReference entries.

The core idea: **an entity protects itself**. No external code can put an entity into an invalid state, because setters are private and modifications happen only through methods that enforce invariants. Notice that the current time (`utcNow`) is passed as a parameter instead of calling `DateTime.UtcNow`, which makes the Domain testable.
The `Campaign` entity enforces invariants 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, and 8 inside its methods:

The `Donation` entity enforces invariants 3, 4, 5, and 8. Notice that the minimum and maximum bounds are **passed in** to it, because `DonationOptions` belongs to Infrastructure and the Domain has no knowledge of it:

**Where are invariants 9 and 10?** Both live in the Domain. **Invariant 10** is in `Category.EnsureCanBeDeleted(hasCampaigns)`: an entity cannot query the database, so the handler runs the query ("Does the category have campaigns?") and passes in the result; the Domain decides and the handler only fetches the fact (see Task 8). **Invariant 9** is modeled by `ISoftDeletable` together with `SoftDeleteInterceptor` (Task 5): every deletion of a campaign becomes a soft delete, making hard-deleting a campaign with donations impossible by design (stronger than the invariant, and satisfies it). And `DeleteBehavior.Restrict` remains a safety net at the database level.

**Why is `ApplicationUser` not in the Domain?** Because it inherits from `IdentityUser<Guid>`, which would make the Domain depend on the Identity package. The common solution: place it in `Infrastructure/Identity`, and reference it from entities via `Guid` only (`CreatedByUserId` and `DonorUserId`).

EF Core will emit a warning because `Campaign` has a query filter while being the required end of a relationship with `Donation`. Understand what this means: when loading a donation belonging to a soft-deleted campaign, the campaign will be missing from the result. The fix is either a matching query filter on `Donation` or handling the case explicitly — document your decision in the README.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 4 — Generic Repository, Unit of Work, and Read Separation

solutionBlocks.markdown: **Writes** go through Repository + UoW so all changes stay within a single transaction and the code remains mockable. **Reads** use `IQueryable` with `AsNoTracking` and direct projection to DTOs, because loading and change-tracking a full entity just to display it wastes memory and CPU.

There is no `Update` method in the Repository: an entity loaded via `GetByIdAsync` is already **tracked**, and any change to it is saved on `SaveChangesAsync`. Calling `Update` causes EF to mark all columns as modified unnecessarily.

To use `ToListAsync` and `AnyAsync` on `IQueryable` inside Application, you will need the `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` package (without the SQL Server provider). This is an acceptable and common trade-off; the purer alternative is keeping all read queries in Infrastructure behind interfaces. Document your choice in the README.
And the registration in `AddInfrastructureServices` (completed in Task 6):

**`ExecuteDelete` bypasses the Interceptor!** `ExecuteDeleteAsync` and `ExecuteUpdateAsync` send SQL directly and skip the ChangeTracker, so soft delete will not run. Use `Remove` + `SaveChangesAsync` for soft-deletable entities.

solutionBlocks.markdown: `appsettings.json` contains non-secret values only, and secrets are intentionally empty so the app **fails fast** if they are not configured:

solutionBlocks.code:
cd src/DonationHub.Api
dotnet user-secrets init
dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:SecretKey" "<random-string-of-at-least-32-characters>"
dotnet user-secrets set "SeedAdmin:Password" "<Strong-Passw0rd>"
dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:Default" "Server=localhost;Database=DonationHub;User Id=sa;Password=<password>;TrustServerCertificate=True"

solutionBlocks.markdown: Try it yourself: remove `Jwt:SecretKey` from user-secrets and run the app — it must stop immediately with `OptionsValidationException` instead of starting up and crashing on the first login. That is what Fail Fast means.

solutionBlocks.text: Task 7 — Identity, JWT, and Refresh Token Rotation

solutionBlocks.markdown: We use `AddIdentityCore` (without cookies since this is an API), and configure the password policy per IDN-02. Identity stores `NormalizedEmail` in uppercase, so `FindByEmailAsync` searches case-insensitively automatically.

Creating the Access Token and generating the Refresh Token. The Refresh Token is a cryptographically secure random value (64 bytes), and we store **only its SHA-256 hash**, so even if the database leaks, the tokens cannot be used:
In Sprint 1 (before the Result Pattern), we use a temporary exception carrying the error code and HTTP status, which `IExceptionHandler` maps to ProblemDetails:

The heart of authentication. Pay attention to the order in `LoginAsync`: we verify the password **before** checking `IsActive`, otherwise an attacker could learn that an account exists and is deactivated without knowing the password:
Converting errors to RFC 9457 ProblemDetails with a `code` field (simplified version; full version in Sprint 2):
Seeding data at startup — idempotent (running it twice duplicates nothing):

**A trade-off you should know:** deactivating a user immediately blocks them from logging in or refreshing, yet any Access Token they already hold **remains valid until it expires** (15 minutes). That is why we keep its lifetime short. Blocking it immediately requires a per-request check or a token revocation list — which is out of scope for this sprint.
Each use case lives in its own file inside the slice (combined here into one file for brevity). Notice that writes go through UoW, while reads project directly to DTOs:

The Controller is **thin**: it knows no business rules — it simply receives the request, invokes the handler, and returns the appropriate HTTP status code. This is what makes migrating to MediatR in Sprint 2 a straightforward swap.
On .NET 10 (`Microsoft.OpenApi` v2 package), we add a document transformer that defines the Bearer security scheme:

On **.NET 9**, the types live in the `Microsoft.OpenApi.Models` namespace, and the reference is written as `new OpenApiSecurityScheme { Reference = new OpenApiReference { Type = ReferenceType.SecurityScheme, Id = "Bearer" } }`, as shown in Israel Quiroz's video.
Finally, `Program.cs` wires everything together:

solutionBlocks.code:
# DonationHub API

## Prerequisites
- .NET 10 SDK
- SQL Server (local instance or Docker)

## Setup
    cd src/DonationHub.Api
    dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:Default" "<connection-string>"
    dotnet user-secrets set "Jwt:SecretKey" "<32+ random characters>"
    dotnet user-secrets set "SeedAdmin:Password" "<strong password>"
    # development-only test users (Campaign Manager + Donor)
    dotnet user-secrets set "DevSeedUsers:ManagerEmail" "<manager email>"
    dotnet user-secrets set "DevSeedUsers:ManagerPassword" "<strong password>"
    dotnet user-secrets set "DevSeedUsers:DonorEmail" "<donor email>"
    dotnet user-secrets set "DevSeedUsers:DonorPassword" "<strong password>"
    cd ../..
    dotnet ef database update --project src/DonationHub.Infrastructure --startup-project src/DonationHub.Api
    dotnet run --project src/DonationHub.Api

## Try it
1. Open `https://localhost:<port>/scalar`.
2. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` with the seeded admin → copy `accessToken`.
3. Click **Authentication**, paste the token, then call `POST /api/v1/categories`.

## Design decisions
- **Writes vs reads:** commands use Generic Repository + Unit of Work (one transaction, easy to mock);
  queries use `IReadDbContext` with `AsNoTracking()` and project straight to DTOs (no tracking cost, only needed columns).
- **ApplicationUser lives in Infrastructure** so the Domain has zero package dependencies.
- **Refresh tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes** and rotated on every refresh.
- **Login checks the password before IsActive** to avoid revealing which accounts exist.

items: `Domain` contains a `PackageReference` (such as EF Core or Identity) — violates the dependency rule.
Using `DateTime.UtcNow` inside entities instead of passing the current time as a parameter.
Public setters on entities, or business rules inside the Controller.
Returning the entity itself from the API instead of a DTO (leaks `RowVersion`, `IsDeleted`, etc.).
Storing the Refresh Token in plain text, or failing to revoke the old token upon refresh.
Returning different error messages for "email not found" and "wrong password".
Putting `Jwt:SecretKey` or a real password in `appsettings.json` and committing it — even if deleted later, it remains in Git history.
Checking `CategoryId` only on non-deleted campaigns when deleting a category, causing deletion to fail with a 500 FK error instead of 409.
Forgetting `base.OnModelCreating(builder)` in `AppDbContext`, causing Identity table configurations to be lost.

solutionBlocks.text: Questions to Prepare For in the Review

items: Why do reads bypass the Repository while writes go through it? What do we gain and what do we lose?
What is the difference between an Entity and a Value Object? And why does `Money` compare by value?
Why do we store a hash of the Refresh Token rather than its raw value? And why is SHA-256 sufficient here without needing bcrypt?
What happens if someone steals a Refresh Token and uses it before its legitimate owner? (Think about IDN-13)
Why is `DbContext` Scoped while `SoftDeleteInterceptor` and `TimeProvider` are Singleton? And when does a Singleton become dangerous (Captive Dependency)?
Why do endpoints return 404 rather than 403 for non-owned resources? (You will need this in Sprint 3)
What happens if `Task.Run` is called around `ToListAsync`?

solutionBlocks.markdown: **IDN-13 (Reuse detection):** If a **revoked** (not merely expired) token is presented, that signals theft. Walk the `ReplacedByTokenId` chain, revoke all active tokens in the family, and return `Auth.RefreshTokenInvalid`:
**Early unit tests:** Testing invariants in the Domain is very easy because the current time is passed as a parameter:

If your solution upholds the same **principles** (unidirectional dependencies, self-protecting entities, secrets outside Git, read/write separation, hashed and rotated tokens), you are on the right track even if the details differ.
